A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiP framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Corresponding material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model and multimodal evaluations, latency and memory measurements, ablations, and attention-distribution analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds attention-distribution results for additional model families.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 and Algorithm 1 correct the initial chunk bounds from round(jT/k), round((j+1)T/k)-1 to round((j-1)T/k)+1, round(jT/k), for j=1,...,k. This locally corrects the specified initialization. The hierarchical selection, block approximation, offloading, and previously presented ensemble procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The datasets and tasks remain unchanged, including PG19, WikiText2, passkey retrieval, RULER, LongBench, BookSum, MMLU, multimodal benchmarks, and Arxiv healing. The added model-family diagnostics use existing datasets and do not introduce different task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 7 adds a separately evaluated H2O (stream) curve alongside H2O. The comparator membership in the main benchmark tables and retained appendix comparisons is otherwise unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 extends the diagnostic evaluation from Llama3.1-8B to Qwen2-7B and Exaone-3.0-7.8B, with model-specific layer and head selections. These are additional model configurations using the existing distribution-fitting procedures; the retained benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 substantially broadens empirical checks of the theoretical assumptions across model families: normality, attention-score means, logarithmic standard-deviation fits, and fit-error heatmaps now include Qwen2 and Exaone. A new close examination of Qwen2 outliers tests an exception to the Gaussian approximation. Existing ablations and ensemble analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. The added KL-divergence and NRMSE results extend existing diagnostic procedures without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new statistical estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figure 7 substantially changes reported baseline findings: the roughly 60–75 perplexity, crashing curve labeled H2O in v2 is labeled HyperAttention with ld=3 in v3. v3 shows separate H2O and H2O (stream) curves around 9–11 perplexity. Appendix A.3 also adds model-specific results, including Qwen2 examples with KL divergence above 1. These are reporting changes, not established same-setting performance gains; Tables 1–6 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the initial chunk intervals is corrected in Section 3.1 and Algorithm 1 to cover indices 1 through T. The locality assumptions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs otherwise remain unchanged; the expanded Appendix A.3 supplies empirical support rather than new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free hierarchical attention, O(T log T) attention computation, hardware-aware sparsity, and KV-cache offloading with favorable quality and efficiency.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly discusses Qwen2's high-KL exceptions, attributes their discontinuous distributions tentatively to internal model operations, and argues that their rarity and approximately Gaussian shape preserve the approximation's usefulness. Existing qualifications about nonzero means, dependence, and late-iteration failures remain.

D1.justification: Table 11 adds checkpoint identifiers and context limits for Gemma2-2B-it, Gemma2-9B-it, and Exaone3-7.8B. The new Figure 19 documents program-level organization, top-k synchronization, and memory hierarchy. Hardware, healing settings, and code-access instructions are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Section 2 and Appendix E.1 are unchanged. Bibliographic differences primarily reflect updated page references.

P1.justification: Appendix A.3 is locally reorganized, its separate empirical-analysis subsection is absorbed into the discussion, and Appendix B gains a flow-diagram subsection. Other changes include limited prose and caption edits, expanded acknowledgements, and the ICLR publication header; the main narrative remains largely verbatim.

P2.justification: Several Appendix A.3 figures expand from single-model displays into extensive multi-model panels, accompanied by a new Qwen2 outlier figure and the detailed HiP flowchart in Figure 19. Figure 7 revises its curves and legend, Table 11 gains rows, and figures and tables are repositioned throughout the document.

improvement.justification: The broader assumption checks and explicit Qwen2 exceptions make the empirical support more informative. Corrected chunk indices, added checkpoint identifiers, and the detailed flowchart improve precision and reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains: the core proofs and benchmark tables remain stable, while the unexplained Figure 7 revisions and unresolved distributional approximations limit the overall improvement.
